title: Canadian CT Head Rule
keywords: suspected open or depressed skull fracture
sources: Stiell IG et al. Lancet 2001; Stiell IG et al. JAMA 2005 (validation)
purpose: Identifies which adults with minor head injury (witnessed LOC, amnesia, or disorientation AND a GCS of 13–15) need a CT head. It is 100% sensitive for neurosurgically important injury and ~98–100% sensitive for any clinically important injury. Any positive item = CT.

items.label: HIGH RISK — GCS < 15 at 2 hours after injury
HIGH RISK — Suspected open or depressed skull fracture
HIGH RISK — Any sign of basal skull fracture (haemotympanum, raccoon eyes, CSF oto/rhinorrhoea, Battle's sign)
MEDIUM RISK — Retrograde amnesia to the event ≥ 30 minutes
MEDIUM RISK — Dangerous mechanism (pedestrian struck, occupant ejected, fall from > 3 ft / 5 stairs)

interpretation.label: No criteria — CT head not required by the rule. Observe, give head-injury discharge advice, and use clinical judgement (the rule was NOT derived for patients on anticoagulants — image them regardless)
≥ 1 criterion — obtain a non-contrast CT head. A HIGH-RISK criterion predicts need for neurosurgical intervention; a MEDIUM-RISK criterion predicts a clinically important brain injury on CT

notes: Inclusion: blunt head trauma with witnessed LOC, definite amnesia, or witnessed disorientation, AND initial GCS 13–15, AND injury within 24 h. EXCLUSIONS (rule does not apply — use judgement / image): age < 16, anticoagulation or bleeding disorder, seizure after injury, GCS < 13, no LOC/amnesia/disorientation, obvious penetrating trauma or depressed fracture, acute focal neuro deficit, unstable vitals, pregnancy. Compared with the New Orleans Criteria, CCHR is more specific (fewer CTs) at equal sensitivity for important injury.
buildNote: Rule — any positive item mandates CT; the count is not a graded risk.
